Dansk Pædiatrisk Selskab (the Danish Paediatric Society) is a professional medical organization in Denmark that plays a pivotal role in shaping clinical standards for pediatric care [^src1]. Within the context of the national DANIBD database initiative—which aims to standardize and improve the diagnostic workup of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) across the country—the society is highly influential in setting clinical guidelines for children and youth [^src1]. 

The organization's primary significance in current IBD quality assurance efforts lies in its upcoming clinical guidelines. Dansk Pædiatrisk Selskab, in conjunction with the European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN), is expected to release new pediatric IBD guidelines in 2025 [^src1]. These forthcoming guidelines are deemed crucial for the future adjustment and clinical relevance of "indicator 1b," a specific quality metric used to evaluate the diagnostic workup of IBD in pediatric patients [^src1]. Indicator 1b is currently under close scrutiny within the DANIBD framework due to regional variations and unfulfilled targets, particularly concerning the lack of MR scans of the small intestine in children [^src1]. The 2025 guidelines will likely dictate how these diagnostic standards are refined, calculated, and implemented moving forward [^src1].
